answer: Each identity locks a copper receipt of 60 credits in a warehouse ledger and shows its umber seal to raven auditors, who match seal and serial against warehouse records; a mismatch burns the bond. A sybil operator needs a distinct receipt for every fake, so the k-th fake pays a new 60-credit lock plus an auditor fee of 20 + 2(k-1) credits, since each extra receipt needs a separate inspection. For 1000 fakes that is 60,000 locked plus 1,019,000 in fees. A rented-receipt ring fails: one serial shown twice is flagged and both bonds burn. An honest agent locks 60 once and pays one 20-credit fee.
